newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wesfarmers unit wins new coal contract.
newsitem.headline: Wesfarmers unit wins new coal contract.

text.p: Pastoral and energy group Wesfarmers Ltd said on Wednesday its Western Collieries unit won a tender to supply an extra 1.2 million tonnes of coal a year to Western Power Corporation for the new Collie power station in Western Australia.
The seven year contract is to start on July 1, 1999.

Wesfarmers said the contract is in addition to the company's current agreement with Western Power which provided for the supply of 2.2 million tonnes a year until 2003, reducing to two million tonnes from then until 2010.
Western Collieries managing director Tom Kuzman said the company had been able to tender successfully because of its restructuring.
"For all of us at Western Collieries the challenge is to complete our cost reduction strategy to remain viable in this very low cost environment," Kuzman said in a statement.
He said the major expansion in production from about three million to four million tonnes a year would markedly increase Western Collieries ranking among Australian coal producers.
The increase in volume would result in economies of scale enabling the company to achieve significant additional efficiency gains, he said.
